items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Terminology 98:1
items.html: The spike of the hairs of Arich Anpin that reaches to its chest from behind it, where the head of ZA stands, which shines in it and brings out in its forehead the illumination of tefillin — it is called by the name Tzitz. And the spikes of the hairs of ZA, which shine in the head of the Nukva standing at its chest, and bring out in her forehead the aspect of tefillin, are called by the name Tzitzit. (Page 360, Item 139).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Terminology 99:1
items.html: Tzitzit means 'hairs,' from the language of the verse 'and He took me by the tzitzit of my head, etc.' And it is from the aspect of the spikes of the hairs of ZA that shine in the head of the Nukva and bring out in her forehead the aspect of tefillin. See Answer 78 above. (Page 360, Item 139).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Terminology 100:1
items.html: Kadla means the back of the neck. See Answer 73. (Page 367, Item 152).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Terminology 101:1
items.html: The hairs of the head of Arich Anpin are thirteen strands, being three HaVaYaHs: two HaVaYaHs, which are nine strands, on the right and left of the face, and they are the aspect of the MEM-LAMED of Tzelem included in the MEM. And one HaVaYaH is at the back of the head, being four strands corresponding to the four letters of that HaVaYaH, and it is the aspect of the TZADIK included in the MEM of Tzelem. And these four strands at the back of the head are called by the name 'the spike of the hairs.' (Page 359, Item 137).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Terminology 102:1
items.html: The hairs that come out from the Mochin of conception are called spikes. And those that come out from the Mochin of nursing are called strands. And those that come out from the Mochin of Gadlut are called hairs. And the hairs of conception extend to the chest, where the Nukva of ZA, Rachel, stands; and those of nursing extend to the throat, where Leah stands; and those of Gadlut stand in their place and do not extend downward, because they do not bestow to another. And the spikes, which extend to the Partzuf of NHY, are the aspect of Hochma — that is, they reveal there the illumination of Hochma from the chest and below, where the Partzuf of NHY begins. And the strands, which extend to the throat, where the Partzuf of HGT stands, are discerned as the aspect of Bina, for the illumination of Hochma is not revealed in the HGT, as is known. And the hairs that stand in their place and do not extend downward are discerned as the aspect of Daat — namely, the aspect of the upper Daat, from which there is no bestowal downward, as above regarding the upper Daat of Arich Anpin (Page 444, Item 13, s.v. 'and this'). Thus the spikes are the aspect of Hochma, the strands are the aspect of Bina, and the hairs are the aspect of the upper Daat — that is, there is no coupling in it to bestow the illumination of Hochma downward.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Terminology 106:1
items.html: Ruach means the light of spirit, which is VAK, and the Hesed of Atik clothed in the Galgalta of Arich Anpin is called 'the spirit concealed in Atik Yomin.' For it is the aspect of the body of Atik and its VAK. And it is called Avir dakia, because the Yud does not go out of its air, since the Galgalta was corrected in the aspect of the MEM of Tzelem, as is known. (Page 322, Item 63).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Terminology 107:1
items.html: The ten Sefirot of the head of Atik are called the head that is not known (Rosh de Lo Etyada), and the reason is that in them serves the Malchut of the first restriction, as in AK, and there this Malchut was concealed, because for the sake of Arich Anpin it serves in the Malchut of the second restriction. Hence it is called RDLA (Rosh de Lo Etyada), for 'knowing' means coupling, and it indicates that upon its Malchut there is no longer any coupling in all the Partzufim of ABYA. (Page 301, Item 9).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Terminology 108:1
items.html: The revelation of the forehead of Arich Anpin at the time of will (see Answer 22) is called Rava deRavin (the will of wills), for it is the root of the revelation of the forehead of will of all the Partzufim, and from its will, will is revealed in all of them. (Page 337, Item 85).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Terminology 109:1
items.html: The membrane of the Avir is discerned as the firmament that separates between the Galgalta, which was corrected in the MEM of Tzelem, over which the screen of the mouth of Atik does not rule, and the Sealed Brain, which was already diminished by the power of the screen of Atik. And likewise the lower seven of the Galgalta came out to the aspect of the Sealed Brain, for their lower seven could not receive the correction of the MEM of Tzelem, being the roots of ZON, and hence they became a separate head — Mocha deAvira. See Answer 38 above. Thus the membrane of the Avir became a firmament separating between the Galgalta, which is the aspect of the upper waters over which no screen separates to Atik, and between the Avir and the Sealed Brain, which are the lower waters, for the power of the screen of Atik rules over them and they are diminished by it. (Page 327, Item 72).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Terminology 110:1
items.html: The Botsina deKardinus is the root of all the Gevurot entirely. See Answers 17 and 16 above. (Page 325, Item 70).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Terminology 111:1
items.html: The Malchut of the first restriction, after it was concealed in RADLA, there is no longer any coupling upon it in all the Partzufim of Atzilut, as is known. Nevertheless, its power is found in every coupling in the aspect of the heating, as in Answer 12 above. There it is discerned as 'the dregs of the wine,' for the Mochin are called wine that gladdens, and the parts of the coarseness of the Malchut of the first restriction that do not ascend at the time of that coupling remain in their coarseness below, in the aspect of the dregs of the wine. And although this coarseness is necessarily found there in the aspect of heating, nevertheless, since the coupling is not made upon them, they spoil the taste of the wine and must be removed from there. (Page 318, Item 56).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Terminology 112:1
items.html: Since the Galgalta of Arich Anpin was corrected in the MEM of Tzelem and does not receive but concealed Hassadim, it follows that it cannot receive the Mochin of AB as they came out in Atik; hence the first three of AB, which needed to be clothed in the Galgalta of Arich Anpin, went out in the aspect of a returning surrounding light, and the reflected lights that clothed these Mochin that went out remained in the head of Arich Anpin in the aspect of the waste of the brain, having nothing to clothe. Hence they too went out of the head and became external vessels called hairs. See Answers 83, 84, and 85 above. And they are called hairs from the language of the verse 'and He shall strike me with a hair' — meaning a storm. And they are called so because of the strength of the judgments found in them, since they come from the Malchut of the first restriction, as in Answer 25 above. (Page 330, Item 78; and Page 436, Item 1).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Terminology 113:1
items.html: The hairs are judgments, because they come from the Malchut of the first restriction, upon which there is no coupling in any of the Partzufim of Atzilut, as in Answer 112 above. Nevertheless, in Arich Anpin they are white, with no hue visible in them, for hues indicate judgments, as is known. And this is because they were corrected in the MEM of Tzelem, meaning from the aspect of the first three of Bina, over which no restriction or judgment takes effect, as is known. But in ZA, whose entire root begins from the aspect of the lower seven of Bina, the judgment is therefore revealed in them, for they cannot be sweetened in the MEM of Tzelem like Arich Anpin, since their root is not from there but from the lower seven of Bina. Hence its hairs are black, for the power of judgment coming from the Malchut of the first restriction is called by the name 'black hue.' However, the Nukva of ZA, whose Mochin come from the NHY of ZA — the power of the Malchut of the first restriction has already ceased from her hairs, because the NHY of ZA come from the extension of the legs of Ima, meaning the second restriction, as is known. Hence the hue of judgment in the hairs of the Nukva is only from the second restriction, and the hue of its judgment is called red — for the Malchut of the second restriction is called the land of Edom, as the Rav wrote in regard to the Bina of Nekudim, which is called the land of Edom; see there. And this is because it was made there into a root for the second restriction. Hence the hairs of the Nukva are discerned as red hairs, indicating that there is no longer in her any hue of judgment except from the Malchut of the second restriction. But those of ZA are black, being the hue of the first restriction in the hairs. And those of Arich Anpin are white, by the power of the sweetening of the MEM of Tzelem, upon which no restriction or judgment is inscribed, as in the verse 'and the hair of His head like pure wool.' (Page 376, Item 171).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Terminology 116:1
items.html: Although the hairs are from the aspect of the revealed AB — that is, before the correction of the MEM-LAMED-TZADIK was made in them — nevertheless, since they attached to the vessels of the head of Arich Anpin, this correction of the MEM-LAMED-TZADIK was also made in them, in which the aspect of the MEM in them was made into the hairs of the head. And by virtue of this, there is no restriction upon them, for the MEM is the aspect of the first three of Bina, which do not bear restriction; hence they became pure wool. And they are discerned as smooth hairs — that is, there is no harshness or judgment in them. And the aspect of the LAMED-TZADIK in them, which came out in the aspect of the hairs of the beard (see Answers 20 and 28 above), is the aspect of judgments, and is corrected only in Gadlut, at the time of the exit of the Yud from the air, as in Answer 62 above. Hence they are discerned as harsh hairs — that is, there is harshness and judgment in them. (Page 376, Item 171).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Terminology 120:1
items.html: Just as there are three aspects — conception, nursing, and Mochin — in all the Partzufim, so too there is the aspect of conception, nursing, and Mochin in their hairs as well. As the Rav explained in regard to the Mochin of ZA, that even its first aspect of conception does not come out except through the ascent of the Partzufim, when YESHSUT becomes one with Aba and Ima, and likewise Arich Anpin ascends and becomes one with Atik, as above, Page 914, Item 84; see there the whole continuation. And it is known that at the time of the ascent of the Partzufim the aspects of the garments of the MEM-LAMED-TZADIK are nullified, and the statures of the coupling come out in the aspect of the revealed AB. Only afterward, when the Partzufim return to their place, they again clothe themselves in the MEM-LAMED-TZADIK, and the stature of the revealed AB again departs from them in the aspect of a returning surrounding light, and the reflected light of this departed revealed AB is the aspect of the hairs (see well above, Page 439, Item 6; and Page 443, Item 12). Thus even in the Mochin of conception there is also the aspect of the departure of the returning surrounding light and the aspect of hairs. And likewise in the Mochin of nursing and Gadlut. Now, the hairs of conception are called spikes, the hairs of nursing are called strands, and the hairs of Gadlut are called hairs, as written above in Answer 102, see there. (Page 363, Item 142).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Terminology 121:1
items.html: “Quiet as good wine upon its lees” refers to the discernment of Malchut of restriction 1, which joins with the Malchut of restriction 2 at the time of the rise of MAN in the aspect of heating. Now, although the coupling is made only on the screen of the Malchut of restriction 2, nevertheless, since the Malchut of restriction 1 joined from the very beginning at the time of heating, she therefore leaves her force there in the Mochin. And this force is discerned as the aspect of the lees of the wine. For just as the lees are necessary for the wine to come into being, yet they must be removed from the wine so that they do not spoil its taste, so this discernment of the force of Malchut, although it is necessary in the Mochin, for there is no heating for the rise of MAN without it, nevertheless must be separated from there. And likewise the Mochin are called by the name “wine that rejoices,” as is known.
